summary: Round 2 verification of Task 7 fixes. The BOT-STORE-001 fix (project-keyed inFlight + identity check at all three call sites — success, 404, finally) is correctly wired for the basic A->B race: the late-arriving fetch for the prior project no longer stomps current. The new regression test at bot.spec.ts:206-228 exercises that path. Intentionally-skipped findings (002/003/004/TYPES-001) are not re-litigated. One new correctness issue surfaces in a narrow rapid-switching window (A->B->A) because the identity check keys on projectId, not on the run's own promise reference — an older run for the same project can wipe the newer run's inFlight slot and write stale data. Round 2 also introduced a defensive token-redaction block in connect(); it works against ofetch's FetchError shape (covered by a new test) but does not redact when ofetch has already stringified the body. Status: changes_required for the A->B->A regression; the rest of the fix is correct.

findings.description: The Round 1 fix keys inFlight by projectId rather than by the run's own promise identity, which introduces a new race in the A -> B -> A rapid-switch window. Trace: (T0) fetch('a') sets inFlight = {'a', run_a}; (T1) fetch('b') overwrites inFlight = {'b', run_b}; (T2) fetch('a') again — projectId !== 'b' so a new run is scheduled and inFlight = {'a', run_a2}; (T3) the original run_a resolves. Inside run_a's success branch (line 17) and finally (line 27) the check `inFlight?.projectId === projectId` is `'a' === 'a'` and passes — even though the entry now points at run_a2's promise, not run_a's. Consequences: (a) run_a writes its potentially-stale data into current.value, overwriting whatever run_a2 may have written, and (b) the finally clears inFlight to null, wiping run_a2's slot. A subsequent fetch('a') from the watcher or the UI no longer dedups against run_a2 (it starts a third run) and run_a2's eventual resolution finds `inFlight === null` and silently drops its result. The window is narrow (requires a switch back to a project while its first fetch is still in flight), but the watcher fires synchronously on every currentProjectId change, so a user double-clicking projects in the sidebar or any code path that re-selects a project programmatically can hit it. The round-1 regression test at bot.spec.ts:206-228 covers only the A -> B case and does not catch this.
findings.recommendation: Switch the identity check from projectId to promise reference. Capture `const run = (async () => {...})()` then guard each call site with `if (inFlight?.promise === run)` — for the success write, the 404 write, AND the finally clear. This is the same idea (a stale-guard token captured at action-entry) but uses a strictly more precise key: the run's own promise. Reference equality is correct under every rapid-switch interleaving because each IIFE produces a unique promise object. Add a regression test mirroring the round-1 one but with the A -> B -> A sequence: start fetch('a') (pending), selectProject('b') (pending fetch('b')), selectProject('a') (new pending fetch('a2')), resolve the original 'a' fetch with stale data, then resolve 'a2' with fresh data; assert current.value ends as the fresh data and that inFlight either still holds 'a2' or has been cleared by 'a2' specifically.
